questions.question: What does createPortal do?
options: Moves a component to a different position in the React tree
Renders children into a different DOM node while keeping them in the React tree
questions.explanation: Only the DOM position changes. The component keeps its place in the React tree, so context and error boundaries still apply.

questions.question: Where does a click inside a portal bubble to?
options: Only to the DOM node it was rendered into
Up the React tree, so React parents receive it
questions.explanation: React events follow the React tree. A click inside a portalled modal reaches handlers on the component that rendered the portal.

questions.question: Which CSS problem does a portal solve?
options: An ancestor's overflow, transform or stacking context clipping or trapping a popup
questions.explanation: Those ancestor properties cannot be overridden from the child. Rendering into document.body removes the modal from that subtree entirely.

questions.question: What does a portal NOT give you for a modal?
options: The ability to render into document.body
Focus management, Escape handling and scroll locking
questions.explanation: Accessibility is a separate job. A portal only changes where the DOM nodes go.

questions.question: Why does Strict Mode render components twice in development?
options: To reveal components that are impure - that change something outside themselves while rendering
questions.explanation: A pure component produces the same result twice with no side effects. Anything that doubles is doing work it should not be doing during render.

questions.question: Your effect runs twice in development. What is the correct response?
options: Add a ref guard so it only runs once
Add cleanup so the effect can be safely set up and torn down repeatedly
Move the code into the render body
questions.explanation: The double mount is checking your cleanup. Any remount in production hits the same path, so the fix is a proper teardown, not suppressing the check.

questions.question: What is useInsertionEffect for?
options: Injecting style rules before layout is calculated, for CSS-in-JS libraries
questions.explanation: It runs before DOM mutations so styles are in place before layout. Application code almost never needs it.

questions.question: When would you use flushSync?
options: When you must read the updated DOM immediately after a state change
questions.explanation: It forces a synchronous render, which is occasionally needed before measuring or scrolling - at the cost of batching and concurrency.
